a.text: There was a mother who once ruled a kingdom until her crown and her family were taken by her foes.

spans.text: There was a mother who once ruled a kingdom until her crown and her family were taken by her foes.

a.text: The mother had a powerful daughter, who then made a pact with the dark mist in the dark woods to drive out their foes. The daughter reclaimed the kingdom for her mother, returning the promised peace to the dark mist.

spans.text: The mother had a powerful daughter, who then made a pact with the dark mist in the dark woods to drive out their foes. The daughter reclaimed the kingdom for her mother, returning the promised peace to the dark mist.

a.text: The mother was to host a grand coronation for her daughter, but the daughter died mysteriously right before the event.

spans.text: The mother was to host a grand coronation for her daughter, but the daughter died mysteriously right before the event.

a.text: Tremendous woe and then rage engulfed the mother. Her zeal to avenge her daughter was so fierce that the entire kingdom was scorched by her vengeful fire.

spans.text: Tremendous woe and then rage engulfed the mother. Her zeal to avenge her daughter was so fierce that the entire kingdom was scorched by her vengeful fire.

a.text: Until that fury disturbed the dark mist, who had just returned to its resting peace.

spans.text: Until that fury disturbed the dark mist, who had just returned to its resting peace.

a.text: The dark mist demanded that the mother cease, or she would be dragged into the darkness. But in her grief, the mother remained convinced that the dark mist was the one who had taken her daughter. A desperate battle was then inevitable. The mother determined to risk her life.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Nemos, Reed...
At the city gates, the nomad looks back at the citadel in the distance one last time.
She resists the urge to turn tail and flee at the acrid burning smell. She knows what it signifies.
She knows she should do as Nemos said, and leave the city to seek the wakemen as quickly as possible, regardless of whether Loughshinny is successful.
But despite the urgency in Nemos's voice, she did not sound like she believed things would take a turn for the better, nor did she believe that Brigid could convince the wakemen to come.
Brigid could smell the same burning smell coming from Nemos. It reminded her of the obsessions that only the dead could have.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Who are you waiting for? Death? Are you just waiting for it to pat you on the back so you can have a nice little race together?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: ...Who is that?

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Oh. I forgot you could hear me.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I can hear you. I can even sense your presence... but I can't see you.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Leave the city, outsider.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: You're an outsider too, by the sound of it.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Naturally. Consider it advice from one outsider to another.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Live, Brigid. Nothing is more important than being alive. This city will be dead by sunrise tomorrow.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Listen to Nemos. Find her kinsmen, run as far as you can, and never look back.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: ...You're right. I should go.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: But I will be back.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Back?!

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Hah! Stubbornness and stupidity really are hereditary!

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: You're going to come back after she tried so hard to get you out of here?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: So you also think it was just an excuse to keep me safe?

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: What else could it be? You really think you can sway those wood-brains? Maybe if you waited for spring, one of their brains would sprout and they might come with you to the Dark Woods!

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: I don't like the way you talk, invisible brother.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: What did you call me? Brother?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: You have burnt stench, but other than that, you remind me of the nomads. No clue how you're related to us, but it feels right.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Haha... hahahahaha!

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Let's make a bet then, Brigid.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: A bet?

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: On whether you'll be back tonight, before Na Saoirsí is burned to the ground. I say it's impossible.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: That's not what you really want to bet on.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Oh yeah? Then tell me, what I'm really thinking?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: You just want to prove that you're right, that nothing is more important than being alive. You think I'll choose survival in the end.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: But whatever. You're on.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Well, what are you waiting for then?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: It just doesn't feel fair. If you win, I'll live the rest of my life in regret. But if I win, it doesn't really matter to a bystander like you.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: So how about this? If I win, you go back to where you came from.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: And where do you think I should go back to?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: No idea, but not here. This isn't your home.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: You sound like you've been betrayed by the cityfolk here before, but you still can't bring yourself to hurt them.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: You act like you want to see them reap what they sowed, but didn't sound happy at all when you talked about the city burning to the ground.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Honestly, you're the most struggling person I ever met, and—

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Enough!

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Very well. If you win, I'll return to where I belong.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: But just coming back here to die won't cut it.

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: What else do you need me to do then?

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Deliver a message to those wood-brains outside the city. Tell them...

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: (Ancient Tengae) 'It's been six hundred years. Nobody's blaming you anymore. Go do your jobs.'

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Oh, and one more thing. (Ancient Tengae) 'I *Ancient Tengae expletive* you stupid wood-brains!'

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Uh... What?

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Pass that on to those fools verbatim, especially the filthier bits. Did you get all that? Need me to repeat myself?

spans.text: Pass that on to those fools verbatim,
the filthier bits. Did you get all that? Need me to repeat myself?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: N-No, the elders sometimes speak that language, so I understand it, more or less...

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: Then go.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: What are you waiting for?

steps.name: Brigid
steps.text: Was all of that just so you could tell me this?

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: ...Just get moving already!
The golden-haired nomad takes a deep breath and runs away from the city.
Her ancestor whose figure she never saw stands in place, unmoving.

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: That stubbornness and stupidity...

steps.name: The Exiled King
steps.text: ...really are hereditary.
Nemos turns to leave, while Loughshinny looks towards the Dark Woods.
The sun has set beneath the horizon. Curfew is about to begin.
In the distance, she sees the dark mist spreading from the forest towards Na Saoirsí, thicker than ever.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*...

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Made it in time...
She raises her spear toward the mist outside, lighting a bright yellow spark in the city of purple.
As though receiving some kind of message, the mist slowly rises until it is level with the flame at the tip of her spear.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Yes, come here, where it's warm and bright, where there's still life... yes, over here.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: What? You want to pretend I don't exist again?

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: I won't let you.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: This light will never go out, not until true darkness falls.
Attracted by the flame in her hand, yet unable to approach, the mist begins to flow through the streets.
Soon, it returns. But this time, her flame can neither draw or repel it.
There is a cacophony within the mist. She feels as though everything has gone dark all of a sudden—
The dark mist has come.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Yes, this is my answer.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: It is incomplete. It needs time.

a.text: Time is your enemy, not your friend.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: We'll see about that.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: The deathly fires have not yet completely transformed the people into the walking dead. They're still alive. There is still time to return the flames.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: And you're not going anywhere until Nemos awakens them.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Ridiculous? Maybe.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: Maybe my strength, my wisdom, and my Arts are all so insignificant to you that it seems ridiculous.

steps.name: Loughshinny
steps.text: But I have my resolve.
Nemos drags the coffin through the corridor.
The red dragon's remains do not burn. They simply lie there quietly.
This is how death should be. But Nemos seems to hear an ethereal voice laughing in her ear.
Without hesitation, the wayward wakewoman lifts the limp body and tosses it into the coffin.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: This coffin, red dragon, is your final resting place...

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: It's where those like you belong.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: So where are you now? Are you still watching us from somewhere, with that twisted smile of yours?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: But this vessel, at least, is beyond your reach. Otherwise, you'd have burned me to ash by now.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: And this spear, which never left your side... How many times have you breathed your flames from it, and how many others like Culann have been your victims?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: You don't even know the answer, do you?
With great effort, Nemos lifts the spear and thrusts it into the coffin.
Flames from its tip engulf the coffin in an instant, spreading along the rope connecting it to Nemos and merging with the purple fire on her.
A deathly cold runs through Nemos's body, but she could hardly feel temperature at this point.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: You're mine now.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I'll finish what Culann started.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Let's go, to those lowly, despicable places that suffered from the war you stole victory in.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: You will be seen by all. Your death will be seen by all.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: They will know that you are dead. That the proud, imperious red dragon is dead. 'Here lies Eblana Dublinn, in this coffin covered in freezing flames.'

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: But... what will they do then?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: I pray that your death will wake them up, of course, as Loughshinny hoped.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: That they'll know that the era you represented is over. That Na Saoirsí will escape this calamity. That Tara need not celebrate its rebirth with the death of a city.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: But... heh...

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Your fire must have gotten to my head, dragon.

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Why is that I suddenly feel like the other ending... where it all ends in destruction... isn't so bad?

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: Someone else may have killed you, but...

steps.name: Nemos
steps.text: This is my revenge.
The coffin remains silent, and Nemos no longer speaks.
Silent, delirious, and determined, she drags the burning coffin down the stairs, making a point to let it hit each step on the way down.
It sounds like the withered mockery of the dead.
